By Mike Allen · Oct 29, 2026

Good Thursday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 672 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to discredit this week's election results by claiming there was mass voting fraud in Arab communities. More from Barak Ravid.
 
 
1 big thing: House Republicans launch Alaska probe
 
Illustration: Maura Losch/Axios

House Oversight Committee Chair James Comer (R-Ky.) is investigating allegations that Democratic operatives recruited an Alaska Senate candidate with the same name as incumbent Dan Sullivan (R) in a bid to siphon votes from him, Axios' Kate Santaliz reports.

  • The probe draws Congress into a controversy surrounding Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign in one of the country's most competitive midterm races.

🔎 Comer is seeking transcribed interviews with Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, as well as Democratic operative Jerid Kurtz.

  • He threatened to use subpoenas to compel testimony from the two Democratic operatives, who were allegedly involved in the recruitment effort.
  • Neither Rios nor Kurtz responded to Axios' requests for comment.

Driving the news: The New York Times reported yesterday that top Peltola campaign staffers directed efforts to track down another Dan Sullivan to enter the race as part of a bid to recruit potential spoilers.

  • The other Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher who will also appear on the ballot, registered as a Republican shortly before the filing deadline.
Early voting yesterday in Anchorage, Alaska. Photo: Nathaniel Wilder/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Both the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee denied involvement in recruiting the other Sullivan, according to the Times.

  • Neither responded to Axios' request for comment.
  • Rios, who was fired amid an August staff upheaval, told the Times that "voters should get the full picture when making their decisions." The newspaper said she later tried to retract her comments for the story.

Go deeper.
 
 
2. 🛒 DoorDash makes case for Instacart deal
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios

DoorDash is seeking to portray its $17 billion Instacart acquisition as a defense of smaller businesses against Amazon and Walmart, Axios' Lucinda Shen reports.

🛍️ The two companies today launched Shop Local Together, where they address potential FTC concerns.

  • Their argument: The combined companies "will have more resources, reach, and technology to help brick-and-mortar grocery stores and retailers compete against the world's biggest e-commerce giants."

🤑 The companies also plan to combine the two services' subscription fees, claiming that will save consumers $100 million annually.

  • They also intend to cancel exclusivity agreements, allowing local grocers to work with any delivery platform.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
The Milwaukee Brewers celebrate winning the Fall Classic in St. Petersburg, Fla., last night. Photo: Kelly Gavin/MLB Photos via Getty Images
  1. ⚾️ The World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers dominated baseball this year in "so many ways," The Athletic writes: 103 regular-season wins, a 16-2 record over their last 18 regular-season games, a postseason sweep against the defending champion L.A. Dodgers, and more. Gift link.
  2. 🔎 A federal investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) "is focused in part on whether she entered into a sham marriage in 2009 to help a man suspected of being her brother obtain a green card," The New York Times reports. Gift link.
  3. 📈 The U.S. economy grew 3.4% in the third quarter, according to government data out today. The economy, supercharged by AI investment and consumer spending, enters the final stretch of the year with remarkable momentum despite the Iran war and high energy prices. More from Courtenay Brown.
  4. 🏈 An estimated 75% of ex-NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had the brain disease CTE, a new study finds. The league told ESPN that it "continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts." Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🥣 1 for the road: Cheerios + Ziploc
 
Photo: General Mills

General Mills is rolling out Cheerios boxes with built-in Ziploc bags to help keep the cereal fresh, Axios Twin Cities' Nick Halter reports.

  • The company, based in the Minneapolis suburb of Golden Valley, said it received hundreds of thousands of letters, emails and DMs asking for an easier way to reseal a cereal box. So General Mills teamed up with Ziploc.

The new Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios boxes are currently a Walmart.com exclusive, but they'll roll out to national retailers in the coming months.
